sections.h2: Who can prepare a quitclaim deed in North Carolina?
sections.html:
In North Carolina, only a licensed attorney may prepare a deed for another person. The definition of practicing law in NCGS 84-2.1 names the preparation of deeds outright, whether or not anyone is paid.

The statute carves out one narrow exception, and it does not reach deeds. A real estate broker acting as agent may select or complete a preprinted form under Real Estate Commission rules, and anyone, including a website provider, may complete a preprinted residential lease. The same subsection says nothing in it lets an unlicensed person or website provider prepare a contract or deed conveying an interest in North Carolina real property, or pass on its title.

The practical result is that an online form service cannot draft your deed for you. Owners who want to sign over their own interest should have a North Carolina attorney prepare it.

sections.h2: What does a quitclaim deed do in North Carolina?
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed passes along whatever interest the signer has, if any, without the signer vouching for the rest. The General Statutes use the word for conveyances and releases of this kind, for example in NCGS 52-10, which lets spouses release and quitclaim rights each may have gained by marriage in the other's property.

That statute adds a formal requirement for real estate. A contract or release between spouses made during the marriage does not affect either spouse's real property unless it is in writing and acknowledged by both before a certifying officer, such as a notary public. The officer cannot be a party to the contract.

Because a quitclaim deed can leave the buyer without promises about title, buyers and lenders usually look harder at the chain of ownership. Ask the closing attorney which type of deed fits your sale and what title search is needed.

sections.h2: Can spouses transfer a house to each other with a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Yes. A conveyance from one spouse to the other of real property the grantor owns alone vests the property in the grantee, and the grantee's spouse need not join in it (NCGS 39-13.3). The deed does not erase every marital right, though.

  • A right to an elective life estate survives unless the deed expressly waives it as G.S. 29-30(a)(2a) allows.
  • A right or claim to equitable distribution under G.S. 50-20 cannot be waived or released in the deed at all.
  • Separation or divorce questions about who keeps the home belong in a separation agreement or court order, which a family law attorney should draft.

Check the loan documents and ask the lender how a change in who holds title affects the mortgage before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed trigger North Carolina excise tax?
sections.html:
It depends on whether anything of value changes hands. The excise tax is $1.00 for each $500, or fraction of $500, of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed, and the transferor pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded (NCGS 105-228.30).

The statute lists transfers that fall outside the tax, including transfers by gift, by intestacy, under a will, by operation of law, and any transfer where no money or property is due from the transferee (NCGS 105-228.29). A quitclaim between family members for no payment typically fits the gift or no-consideration categories, but if a mortgage payoff or cash changes hands, the closing attorney should decide whether tax applies.

Half of the tax goes to the county general fund, and the rest is remitted monthly to the state, so the register of deeds will not record a taxable deed until it is paid.

sections.h2: What must a quitclaim deed look like to be recorded in North Carolina?
sections.html:
The register of deeds checks form and signatures, not legal quality. Under NCGS 47-14 the office will not accept a deed that needs acknowledgment unless the signing appears to have been acknowledged before an officer with apparent authority, and the acknowledgment shows the officer's signature, commission expiration date and seal where required. The register is not required to judge the legal sufficiency of the document or the officer's authority.

sections.h2: Where and when do I record a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Record it with the register of deeds in the county where the land lies. Under NCGS 47-18, a conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value except from the time it is registered in that county, and priority follows the order in which instruments are registered by time.

That rule is the reason not to leave a signed deed in a drawer. If the grantor later signs a second deed or a lender records a lien first, the unrecorded deed can lose. A parcel that sits in two counties is taxed in the county holding the greater value, so ask the register of deeds in that county where to record.

  • Bring the signed, acknowledged original.
  • Bring payment for the recording fee, plus the excise tax if one is due.
  • Bring the information the attorney used to confirm the property description.
  • Keep the stamped copy showing the book, page and recording time.

sections.h2: What should I check before signing a quitclaim deed?
sections.html:
Confirm the record owner, who has to sign, and whether a mortgage or tax lien stays with the house after the transfer. Ask the closing attorney whether a deed of trust or tax lien stays with the house after the transfer.

  • Ask the closing attorney whether the transfer is a gift or involves payment, since that decides the excise tax.
  • Ask the county tax office for the current owner of record and any balance on the tax bill.
  • Check how the existing deed vests title, including whether a spouse also holds an interest.
  • If you plan to sell soon, tell the buyer's closing attorney about the new deed so the title search covers it.

faqs.q: Can I write my own quitclaim deed in North Carolina?
faqs.a: For another person's benefit, no. Preparing deeds is the practice of law under G.S. 84-2.1, and unlicensed persons or website providers may not prepare a deed conveying North Carolina real property. Ask a North Carolina attorney.

faqs.q: Do I pay excise tax on a quitclaim deed to a family member?
faqs.a: Not if the transfer is a gift or no money or property is due from the family member. G.S. 105-228.29 exempts both. If a payment is part of the deal, the $1.00 per $500 rate can apply.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed between spouses end equitable distribution rights?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 39-13.3 says an equitable distribution claim cannot be waived or released in the deed. An elective life estate right also stays unless the deed waives it expressly.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a quitclaim deed in North Carolina?
faqs.a: The general instrument fee is $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for each additional page under G.S. 161-10. A $25.00 extra fee applies if the document is nonstandard, and excise tax is separate.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not record the deed?
faqs.a: The transfer is still signed, but it is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Later recorded interests can take priority over it.
